principles: noindex is not a substitute for consolidation: a page with a valid destination is canonicalized (signals consolidate); noindex discards its signals.
A directive may only be resolved from governance state (publication_authority.py). Templates, renderers and Gate 12-I never choose robots, sitemap or canonical.
Legacy URLs keep at most the directives they were served with (status quo). Every decision type can only downgrade.
Indexation of a new or rebuilt URL requires Contract C index_approved AND Gate 12 PASS (or Gate 12-I PASS + an R11 certification).
No per-URL decision is applied without Search Console evidence for that URL (indexed state, impressions, external links) when the URL is a brand/identity surface or has external links.
Never combine noindex with a cross-URL canonical; never canonicalize to a URL that is noindex, redirected, or not self-canonical.
Textual similarity nominates; identity, destination quality and Search Console concordance decide (Recovery-03).

rules.when: ALL of: (1) same language and same governed entity, with the entity identity verified (governed evidence or a recognized ontology concept); (2) the destination passes Gate 12 or is the canonical route of a governed Knowledge Object; (3) the destination is live, served index and self-canonical; (4) Search Console, when available, does not show Google selecting a different canonical for the duplicate. Raw substantive similarity (e.g. >= 0.80) is a DIAGNOSTIC that nominates candidates; it never authorizes a canonical by itself.
rules.sitemap: remove the duplicate; keep the destination only if approved
rules.reversible: yes: remove the canonical link (head-only change; body hash unchanged)
rules.revised_in: Recovery-03 (2026-10-30): the 0.80 similarity threshold alone is not canonical authority.
rules.eligible_now: 0 of 453 similarity-nominated pairs: all 106 destinations fail Gate 12 and none is a KO canonical route (main/data/recovery/R03_INDEXATION_REDUCTION_PLAN.json).

rules.when: the concept has a shorter existing URL (e.g. /pyrite/) that is not yet a route
rules.decision: register the short URL as the canonical route first; then point duplicates at it
none (status quo) until a valid destination or a rebuilt page exists

rules.when: a canonical concept surface is rebuilt from a Knowledge Object
rules.decision: replace the body in place (same URL); indexation only via Contract C
rules.robots: noindex while repairing (LEGACY_REPAIR_NOINDEX) or Contract C derived
rules.reversible: yes: the sealed baseline keeps the previous body hash; revert the commit

rules.when: seo_class = internal_pipeline_status, or an approved identity review finds a generated entity does not exist
rules.reversible: yes, but re-indexing is slow; requires Search Console check that the URL had no impressions/links

rules.when: a release authority denies the URL (release_ledger blocked) while it is served index
rules.decision: owner decides: authorize release in the ledger, or noindex
rules.robots: resolver enforces noindex until the ledger changes

rules.when: a URL has no independent value AND an approved indexable destination exists AND the URL has external links or impressions
rules.hosting_constraint: GitHub Pages cannot return HTTP 301/308. A redirect is a static stub (meta refresh 0 + rel=canonical to the destination), which Google generally follows but which is weaker than a server redirect. Prefer rel=canonical while the source still holds duplicate content; use stubs only for retired URLs; move hosting if many permanent redirects are needed.
rules.reversible: partly: restoring a page after Google processed the redirect is slow

rules.when: generated entity disproven by identity review AND no impressions AND no external links (Search Console)
rules.decision: retire (404); or redirect to the family page if links exist
rules.reversible: yes (restore the file), but lost crawl history is not recoverable

rules.decision: never noindex; rebuild first (homepage preview); indexation authority via Contract C R11 (home) or a governed terminology object (bisulfid pages)

sitemaps are generated only by scripts/publication/generate_sitemaps.py; policy approved_only lists Contract-C index_approved self-canonical URLs; status_quo may never list a URL the live sitemap did not already list
